question: Should ClawHub take ownership of server-hosted cross-device watch and inbox state now, or continue with the client-first watch model until demand, consent, signing, privacy, retention, and abuse requirements are accepted?
rationale: The PR itself identifies unresolved product and operational commitments that cannot be resolved mechanically from the patch, and the repository policy only permits closure when main definitely implements the requested behavior.

options.title: Keep the prototype parked
options.body: Retain this draft as a design reference while client-side watches validate demand and the listed ownership prerequisites remain unresolved.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped server-hosted phase
options.body: Approve a narrower successor plan that first fixes the consent, account-ACL, retention, abuse, signing, migration, and end-to-end proof boundaries.

options.title: Decline server-hosted ownership
options.body: Close the direction only after a maintainer decides that cross-device inboxes are out of scope and documents the client-first boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep the prototype parked
recommendation.body: Retain this draft as a design reference while client-side watches validate demand and the listed ownership prerequisites remain unresolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author recorded the concrete deferred conditions and can provide the prototype context, while a repository product owner must make the final acceptance decision.
